design.transport: strict JSON; JSON Schema 2020-12 describes structure but schema validity alone carries no semantic authority
design.identity: domain-separated length-prefixed transcript over typed digest tokens; no arbitrary JSON canonicalization is inside K1 claim identity
design.open_universe: REALIZE may contain any syntactically valid consequence commitment, including a target-native consequence absent from ALLOW
design.claim_authority: W and ALLOW are precommitted in claim_id
design.proof_authority: closure and grounding are proof references, never booleans
design.unknown_proof_kind: structurally valid but semantically unsupported until a checker recognizes and validates that proof kind
design.annotations: not part of W0; explanatory metadata remains outside the kernel wire until a non-authoritative envelope is separately specified

identity_transcript.atom_encoding: netstring: decimal byte length, colon, bytes, comma
identity_transcript.ordering: worlds, relation pairs, grounding entries, and evidence roots are lexicographically sorted by their ASCII typed IDs before hashing
identity_transcript.duplicate_policy: duplicates are invalid, never silently deduplicated

claim_rules: every ALLOW pair references a declared world
every declared world has at least one ALLOW consequence
claim_id is recomputed from semantics, sorted worlds, and sorted ALLOW pairs
there is no closed consequence vocabulary in a claim
certificate_rules: certificate claim_id must equal the supplied valid claim
every REALIZE pair references a declared world
REALIZE may introduce target-native consequence commitments not named by ALLOW
closure_proof is a proof reference object with kind and artifact commitment, not an assertion bit
grounding_proofs may be incomplete at the wire layer; completeness is a checker verdict obligation
certificate_id binds claim, target, REALIZE, closure proof reference, grounding proof references, and evidence roots
witness_rules: a regression witness references one admitted world/consequence pair
the consequence may be target-native and absent from ALLOW
the witness carries a grounding proof reference but no closure proof because one grounded forbidden realization is locally sufficient if the grounding proof is accepted
witness_id binds claim, target, pair, grounding proof reference, and evidence roots
non_authoritative_at_w0: proof artifact contents before a checker validates them
evidence contents before a checker validates their bindings
the statement that a certificate is closed
the statement that a pair is grounded
forbidden_shortcuts: source consequence enum used as a closed universe
post-result mutation of W or ALLOW under the same claim_id
unknown proof kinds treated as accepted authority
next_stage: A tiny independent checker may consume W0 only after W0 identity and malformed-input adversarial vectors pass. The first checker must support an intentionally small proof fragment and return UNKNOWN/ASSURANCE_INCOMPLETE for unsupported proof kinds.
